item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A is materially closer to the frozen contract because it adds the required replayable convenience API while leaving FilesService.Add unchanged. Candidate B explicitly changes Add’s behavior by eagerly reading and buffering every caller-provided body, violating a central compatibility requirement.","reasons":["A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field name \"file\" and the supplied filename, producing the replayable body required for retries.","A preserves the existing Add implementation, signature, and lower-level behavior; B changes Add to consume the entire reader before request construction and introduces new read-error wrapping.","B’s new Add buffering is unnecessary scope expansion and changes memory use, timing, reader-consumption, and error semantics for existing callers.","Neither candidate follows the explicit requirement that Upload route through FilesService.Add: A duplicates Add’s request/response logic, while B routes both methods through a new private add helper. A is nevertheless preferable because it avoids altering the established public method’s behavior."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add’s option, request, decoding, and missing-data logic instead of delegating to Add, creating drift risk and violating the required repository pattern.","The added tests do not visibly cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.","The retry test uses a wrapped strings.Reader rather than an actual os.File and does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods: true."],"risks_b":["Add no longer preserves existing behavior: it eagerly buffers all custom multipart bodies and changes source-reader error semantics.","Upload does not route through Add as required, instead using a newly extracted private helper.","The extra Add retry behavior and test expand scope beyond the requested convenience API and frozen contract constraints attributable to existing callers even when not needed for Upload compatibility—altering memory characteristics for arbitrarily large custom bodies and advancing read failures before request setup/execution begins rather than preserving previous lower-level semantics clearly. Also, like A, B lacks visible validation and source-reader error tests for Upload."]}
